judgments.reasoning_cat1: A cap expressed as 'not to exceed a maximum of $500,000 or 1% of aggregate Principal of outstanding Notes, whichever amount is greater' is self-defeating as a ceiling and floats with the size of the raise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c045 states the identical definition of Company Expenses with no cap at all, so the two versions of the same covenant differ.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Anticipated to average 3%-6%' and 'approximately $1,000-$2,000' set expectations rather than limits, and the closing sentence redirects all borrower fees to the Manager in a delegated structure.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c043 gives the documentation fee as approximately $1,000 per loan, not $1,000-$2,000, and c047's truncated footnote is the only ceiling on the servicing fee.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One sentence allocating Loan Service Expenses to the Servicer; definite.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Construction management fees, development fees, placement fees, loan origination fees, brokerage fees, or other fees' is a catch-all after specifics, and 'subject to restrictions with respect to Affiliated Transactions' invokes a capitalised term that is never defined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'Affiliated Transactions' appears nowhere else in the instrument; the nearest analogues are the Related Party Loan limits at c052-c054 and the criteria 'established by the Note Purchase Agreement' at c076.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The Company will be subject to restrictions in the amount of compensation it may receive' inverts the actual arrangement — the Company pays compensation to the Manager and Servicer — which is a mechanical error that changes the sense.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The restrictions summarised at c037-c046 and c102 are all on compensation the Company pays, confirming the mismatch.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Will terminate at the Manager's election upon the first to occur of' mixes an automatic first-to-occur trigger with a discretionary election, leaving it unclear whether termination is automatic.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is measured off the 'Maturity Date of the Notes', which c089 defines twice and c016 describes as extendable, so the end of the Company term inherits that uncertainty.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Except for certain transfers to family trusts, to wholly-owned affiliates or by operation of law' leaves 'certain' undefined, so the permitted class of transfers cannot be identified from the text.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c004 says the Notes may not be transferred 'except as provided in the Note Purchase Agreement', and c017 describes 'very limited circumstances ... in the discretion of the Manager'; three formulations of one restriction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Senior in priority as to either or both its payment or exercise' is awkward, and the Noteholders' advance agreement to subordination is broad but stated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c109 forbids any Lien on the Collateral without approval of a Majority in Interest 'except as permitted pursuant to the Security Agreement', while this clause has the Noteholders pre-consent to senior liens — the two consent regimes pull against each other, and both cut against c012/c018.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Any of the following, among other restrictions' is an express catch-all appended to an enumerated list, leaving the reach of the consent right uncertain (expressio unius against 'among other restrictions').
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The bar on the Manager withdrawing as sole manager collides with c036's at-will right to terminate the business relationship and c084's power to substitute managers, and the Lien restriction collides with c108's pre-consent to senior borrowings.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'May form one or more new funds ... or similar enterprises to the Company at any time and for any purpose' is garbled ('similar enterprises to the Company') and unlimited.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c056 states the time commitment differently ('only so much time ... as is reasonably required') and c055 imposes an allocation process for competing loan opportunities that this open licence ignores.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Reporting is limited to what is 'reasonably necessary' for tax returns plus whatever the Manager 'in its discretion, may determine', which is soft but deliberately so.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with c112 (Form 1099s only) and c018; no promise of financial statements elsewhere.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'They will receive IRS Form 1099's only on a timely basis' misplaces 'only', so it is unclear whether the limitation is on the form or the timing.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches c018 and c097 (Noteholders are creditors, not members) but presupposes the debt characterisation that c123 and c126 acknowledge may fail.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Words are missing: 'may not be amended without the approval of a Majority in Interest of Noteholders (i) violates the Company's obligations ...' omits the conditional ('if such amendment'), inverting or at least obscuring when consent is needed.
